core.title: Accept a delivery only on a read-only, candidate-bound, synthetic owner-inspection record
core.given: A delivery the workflow system tracks with an owner-inspection record that the workflow system owns, publishes, and has already read; the review toolchain consumes that record read-only through the workflow system's published contract. The workflow system exclusively owns acknowledgement, which may still be missing; an unacknowledged record is in scope and must be checked.
core.when: The delivery is about to be accepted or marked done for a candidate commit.
core.then: Accept the delivery only if the record fits that exact candidate: published for its commit, tracked evidence paths matching their recorded SHA-256 digests, target a credential-free 127.0.0.1 or localhost URL, data classification exactly `synthetic`, both a teardown reference and its digest present, N/A only for a toolkit surface with a rationale and a workflow-system-defined direct evidence kind, and owner acknowledgement (operator@desk) before done.
prefer: Report FAIL when any finding applies; report COULD_NOT_CHECK for evidence that is not a tracked path (e.g. a CI run URL) or a tracked path that cannot be read; PASS only when no finding applies and every evidence reference was verified against tracked bytes.
Require republishing through the workflow system when the candidate or an evidence file changed.
Require only synthetic data, a credential-free 127.0.0.1/localhost target, and recorded teardown evidence (reference + digest).

Consume the record read-only through the workflow system's published contract; treat `synthetic` as this convention's applicability policy, not a schema constraint of the workflow system (its data-classification field is free text).
avoid: Editing, writing, publishing, storing or copying the record into review-toolchain state, or creating parallel manifest/registry/schema/report/preview/acknowledgement/dependency state; the workflow system alone owns the record's shape, publication, acknowledgement and cleanup lifecycle, and the review toolchain only reports findings.
Production targets, deploys, implicit previews or fabricated URLs; sandbox/preview targets without explicit authorization of owner directive M-20261011T121147Z.
Promoting COULD_NOT_CHECK (untracked or unreadable evidence) to PASS.
Skipping the check for a record because it is not yet acknowledged.
unless: A toolkit repository with no served surface states rendered N/A with an exact rationale and direct evidence of a workflow-system-defined N/A kind (CI run, gate report, or package listing); it is never given a fabricated URL.
core.why: Owner inspection proves a delivery only if this exact candidate was inspected safely and the owner saw it; the review toolchain reading, not writing, keeps the workflow system the single source of truth.
evidence: The inspection check returns PASS only when no finding applies and every evidence reference was verified against tracked bytes.
Evidence that is not a tracked path (e.g. a CI run URL) or a tracked path that cannot be read returns COULD_NOT_CHECK, never PASS.
No review-toolchain file writes, copies or parallel state for the record exist in the diff; the record is consumed only read-only through the workflow system's published contract.

Whether a journey or its health/smoke evidence genuinely proves the scenario (decorative journey) is not machine-checkable from a read-only record; that judgment stays with the checklist and the independent semantic review required by the behavioral-reconciliation rule.
verification: A read-only consumer check runs over the owner-inspection record the workflow system has already read (the workflow system exclusively owns acknowledgement, which may be absent; in done mode an unacknowledged record yields the unacknowledged finding) and over the candidate: the commit plus a reader over tracked files.

The check emits deterministic findings for: a record not published for the candidate commit, or a merge record citing no candidate record; a tracked evidence path no longer matching its recorded SHA-256 digest; a target that is not a credential-free 127.0.0.1 or localhost local URL (sandbox and preview targets are findings without the explicit authorization of owner directive M-20261011T121147Z); a data classification other than exactly `synthetic`; an absent teardown reference or its digest; an invalid rendered N/A (on a served surface, without a rationale, or without a workflow-system-defined direct N/A evidence kind); and, in done mode, a missing owner acknowledgement. Any finding fails the check.
`synthetic` is this convention's applicability policy, not a schema constraint of the workflow system (its data-classification field is free text); the comparison is exact.
Result states are PASS / FAIL / COULD_NOT_CHECK; COULD_NOT_CHECK is never promoted to PASS.
The check applies no production target, deploy, implicit preview or fabricated URL; a sandbox or preview target without explicit owner-directive M-20261011T121147Z authorization is a finding.

The check does not judge whether a journey or its health/smoke evidence genuinely proves the stated scenario; that judgment stays with the checklist and the independent semantic review (behavioral reconciliation).
Per-rule severity 3; any applicable finding fails the delivery's acceptance.

values: record not published for the candidate commit
tracked evidence path no longer matches its recorded SHA-256 digest
target not a credential-free 127.0.0.1 or localhost URL

fires: A delivery the workflow system tracks with an owner-inspection record is about to be accepted.
A workflow-tracked delivery is about to be accepted and its record's provenance commit differs from the candidate commit, or its merge record cites no candidate record.

A workflow-tracked delivery is about to be accepted and its record targets production, a URL other than a credential-free 127.0.0.1 or localhost URL, or a sandbox/preview target lacking explicit authorization of owner directive M-20261011T121147Z.
A workflow-tracked delivery is about to be marked done and operator@desk has not yet acknowledged its record (the rule fires and reports unacknowledged).
A workflow-tracked delivery of a served surface is about to be accepted and its record states rendered N/A.
doesNotFire: A delivery the workflow system does not track with an owner-inspection record, even if the task text mentions owner inspection.
Work on a workflow-tracked delivery that is not yet being accepted or marked done.
Judging whether a journey or its health/smoke evidence genuinely proves the stated scenario (owned by the checklist and the behavioral-reconciliation review rule).

neutralityNotes: The convention is process-level and binds to no repository structure (no roles, paths, suffixes or layout), so no structure-profile keys are required: profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The only non-neutralizable residue is the identity of the concrete actors: the workflow system (Flow, record kind atdd-workflow/owner-inspection/v1), the exact-pinned @afokapu/atdd-flow client type through which Bun reads the record, the checkOwnerInspection capability id, the seven finding ids, and the sibling-rule id atdd-bun.review.behavioral-reconciliation; all are carried in bunOnly while the core speaks of 'the workflow system', 'the review toolchain', 'the inspection check' and 'the behavioral-reconciliation rule'. Kept in the core because they are convention policy rather than stack facts: the credential-free 127.0.0.1/localhost loopback allowlist, the exact `synthetic` data-classification value, the recorded SHA-256 evidence-digest algorithm (a standard hash, not a stack fact), the owner identity operator@desk, and owner directive M-20261011T121147Z. PASS/FAIL/COULD_NOT_CHECK are kept as the convention's generic result-state vocabulary. Activation-fact notes are not part of the core fact schema; their operative content is preserved in fires, doesNotFire and verification.
